summary.name: PR Cockpit
summary.one_liner: A keyboard-first macOS and Linux app for reviewing GitHub pull requests from a local cache, so PRs, diffs, threads and checks open almost instantly.
use_cases: Reviewing GitHub pull requests quickly from the keyboard
Triaging open PRs by what needs your attention
Checking failing CI checks and logs before merging
Letting an AI agent wait for PR changes via a CLI
Resolving merge conflicts and open review threads
summary.what_it_does: PR Cockpit is a keyboard-driven app for GitHub pull request review on macOS and Linux. It keeps pull requests, diffs, review threads and checks in a local cache so a PR opens quickly (the page cites 0.020 s). A GitHub webhook marks changed PRs for targeted refresh, and WebSocket invalidations reload the open view from the cache. Open PRs are grouped into lanes such as ready to merge, your move, and waiting. Your comments, reviews and merges show as pending locally until GitHub confirms them, and writes are sent back to GitHub.
notable: Local GitHub cache with webhook-triggered targeted refreshes
pr-cockpit listen command lets an agent wait for PR changes without polling
Three-lane triage sorting open PRs by what needs you
Works alongside JustShowMe and gh-img for visual diffs and PR images
caveats: Live updates go through a relay that is hosted by default; self-hosting is optional
Global shortcuts on Linux depend on the compositor
GitHub remains the authoritative source; this is not a replacement for GitHub
